papers.title: On Sparse variational methods and the Kullback-Leibler divergence between stochastic processes
papers.abstract: The variational framework for learning inducing variables (Titsias, 2009a) has had a large impact on the Gaussian process literature. The framework may be interpreted as minimizing a rigorously defined Kullback-Leibler divergence between the approximating and posterior processes. To our knowledge this connection has thus far gone unremarked in the literature. In this paper we give a substantial generalization of the literature on this topic. We give a new proof of the result for infinite index sets which allows inducing points that are not data points and likelihoods that depend on all function values. We then discuss augmented index sets and show that, contrary to previous works, marginal consistency of augmentation is not enough to guarantee consistency of variational inference with the original model. We then characterize an extra condition where such a guarantee is obtainable. Finally we show how our framework sheds light on interdomain sparse approximations and sparse approximations for Cox processes.

papers.title: An Active Learning Based Approach For Effective Video Annotation And Retrieval
papers.abstract: Conventional multimedia annotation/retrieval systems such as Normalized Continuous Relevance Model (NormCRM) [16] require a fully labeled training data for a good performance. Active Learning, by determining an order for labeling the training data, allows for a good performance even before the training data is fully annotated. In this work we propose an active learning algorithm, which combines a novel measure of sample uncertainty with a novel clustering-based approach for determining sample density and diversity and integrate it with NormCRM. The clusters are also iteratively refined to ensure both feature and label-level agreement among samples. We show that our approach outperforms multiple baselines both on a recent, open character animation dataset and on the popular TRECVID corpus at both the tasks of annotation and text-based retrieval of videos.

papers.title: Selective Laser Melting of Ti-45Nb Alloy
papers.abstract: Ti-45Nb is one of the potential alloys that can be applied for biomedical applications as implants due to its low Young’s modulus. Ti-45Nb (wt.%) gas atomized powders were used to produce bulk samples by selective laser melting with three different parameter sets (energy inputs). A β-phase microstructure consisting of elliptical grains with an enriched edge of titanium was observed by scanning electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction studies. The mechanical properties of these samples were evaluated using hardness and compression tests, which suggested that the strength of the samples increases with increasing energy input within the range considered.

papers.title: Rapid and economic generation of consistent hmsc spheroids for macroscopic tissue biofabrication and therapeutic applications

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文不涉及人工智能在生物打印中的应用。
llm.why_not_core: No AI or machine learning method is employed in any stage of bioprinting workflow.

summary_zh.motivation: 快速经济地生成一致的人间充质干细胞球体用于组织制造。
summary_zh.method: 采用悬滴法和旋转培养等方法形成干细胞球体。
summary_zh.result: 生成的球体大小一致，可用于宏观组织构建。
summary_zh.validation: 通过显微镜观察和细胞活力检测验证球体质量。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a rapid and cost-effective method for producing uniform hMSC spheroids for macroscopic tissue biofabrication and therapeutic applications.
summary_en.method: A combination of hanging drop and rotational culture techniques was employed to generate consistent spheroids.
summary_en.result: Uniform spheroids with high cell viability were produced, suitable for assembling into larger tissue constructs.
summary_en.validation: Spheroid size distribution, morphology, and cell viability were assessed using microscopy and live/dead assays.
